g.text: AI.IF is in an ephemeral model. The call runs again on every read, so the bill
Materialize the AI call as a table or an incremental model, and let later
models read the stored result. A view runs the call again on every read.

Add a WHERE clause, or build a smaller upstream model, so only the rows that
This incremental model calls AI.GENERATE but does not skip rows that already
have a generated value. The next run sends those rows to the model again.
Exclude keys already stored in {{ this }} before the AI call. NOT EXISTS, a
left join that keeps only null matches, or a watermark against {{ this }} all
work. unique_key alone still sends every source row to the model.
AI.GENERATE does not set a thinking budget or thinking level. Thinking tokens
are billed at the output token rate.
Set thinking_config.thinking_budget in model_params. Use 0 when the task does
not need reasoning. On newer models, set thinking_config.thinking_level instead.
LIMIT or OFFSET sits outside AI.GENERATE. The function runs for the rows that
reach the SELECT list, and the clause applies only after that.
Filter with WHERE, write those rows to a table, and read that table from the
AI function. LIMIT inside the prompt query still processes the input first, and
LIMIT on the outer SELECT runs after the function.
ML.GENERATE_TEXT reads a prompt query that uses LIMIT or OFFSET. BigQuery
processes that input before it applies the clause, so the clause does not cut
Filter with WHERE, write those rows to a table, and read that table from the
AI function. LIMIT inside the prompt query still processes the input first, and
LIMIT on the outer SELECT runs after the function.
AI.GENERATE is fed SELECT *. Every column is packed into the prompt and billed
Pass only the columns the prompt needs, for example a CONCAT of the text
fields. Every extra column is billed as input.
AI.GENERATE does not set an output token cap. The response can run long, and
you pay for every output token.
